title: Instagram DM Setter - Paid 30-Day Trial (Sports Vision Training)
description:
ABOUT US

Shah NeuroVision trains athletes' vision, reaction and decision speed, working with everyone from invested youth athletes and their parents to college and professional players. Our Instagram is where most of our new athletes find us, and we're building a small DM team to handle those conversations.



THE ROLE

You'll run conversations in our Instagram DMs, writing from our account in our voice. You'll reach out to people who already engage with our content, learn what they're working toward, and guide the right ones to a free assessment or an evaluation. An AI tool helps draft replies; you step in wherever a real human touch is needed and keep every conversation accurate, friendly and pressure-free.



HOW THE TRIAL WORKS

We're hiring three setters for a paid 30-day trial. Each setter earns base pay for the trial plus $30 for every evaluation they book. At the end of the 30 days, we keep the setter with the best results and offer them the ongoing role, with the same $30 bonus per evaluation.



WHAT YOU'LL DO EACH DAY

- Review our story viewers, likers and commenters, and send about 30 personalized openers a day using each person's name and sport.

- Follow up once on unanswered openers, then close them out.

- Ask good questions to find the athlete's goals and the main thing holding them back.

- Once there's a real need, share the right next step (our video or our free Decision Speed Snapshot) in a no-pressure way.

- Point people to the free resources in our bio.

- Flag anything outside your lane to the owner: health or medical questions, verified or pro accounts, and anyone who may be under 18 (confirm who is writing first).

- Log every conversation in our DM tracker and send a short weekly summary.



WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

- Excellent written English that sounds natural and warm, never scripted.

- Clear, confident spoken English. You may hop on short sales calls with US parents and athletes to help them book.

- A daily Instagram user who is comfortable with DMs, stories and profiles.

- Experience as an appointment setter, DM setter or social media VA (preferred).

- Interest in sports. Knowing baseball, softball, football, basketball, soccer, tennis or cricket is a plus.

- Comfortable working with AI tools and Google Sheets.

- Reliable internet and a quiet place to work.

- Available during US Pacific business hours (8 AM to 12 PM PT).



SCHEDULE AND PAY

- Hours: part-time, 20 hours a week

- Pay: $5 to $6 per hour + $30 for each evaluation you book

- Openings: 3 setters for a paid 30-day trial. The top performer is kept on for the ongoing role.

- Start date: As soon as possible



HOW TO APPLY

Apply through OnlineJobs.ph and include all of the following. Applications missing any part won't be reviewed.

1. Start your message with the words VISION SETTER so we know you read the whole post.

2. A short intro: your setter or DM experience and the sports you follow.

3. Answers to these three questions:

   a) A parent of a high school pitcher just liked one of our reels. Write the exact opener you would send.

   b) Someone's first reply is "how much does it cost?" What do you write back?

   c) A conversation goes quiet after two messages. What do you do?

title: Short Form Editor
description:
Shah Neurovision Sports Training (NeuroVision Edge) teaches athletes the vision and brain side of performance — reaction time, tracking, game IQ. We publish educational Reels on Instagram 
 28K+ followers and climbing). Our content is calm, credible, and genuinely useful — not hype, not motivational fluff. We're scaling our output on a clear path toward 1M followers, and the editor is the engine that makes that possible.

What you'll do

Edit 14–15 short-form videos per week — Instagram Reels, 30–60 seconds, from raw talking-head footage.

Cut podcast footage into Reels — pull standalone clips from our podcast episodes.

Add clean animated captions and text overlays, accurately synced to the audio.

Edit for retention — simple b-roll, zooms, and hard cuts that hold attention, especially in the first 3 seconds.

Build on-screen graphics — hook text, simple stat/drill callouts, and a closing “save this” card.

Light cleanup — basic color and audio so every video looks and sounds sharp.

Export to spec — 9:16, correct resolution, delivered on an agreed schedule.

Hold the format — keep a consistent look across every video using our template.

The format you'll work in

So you know exactly what you're signing up for: our Reels are not complex VFX projects. They're talking-head delivery, animated captions, athlete famous or current athlete events b-roll, and simple text graphics. The skill we care about is retention editing — pacing, cuts, and hook framing — not motion-design wizardry. Once you know our template, each video should be fast to turn around. We'll give you a clear style guide and example videos to match.

What we're looking for

2+ years editing short-form video (Instagram Reels, TikTok, or YouTube Shorts).

A portfolio of short-form work — send your strongest Reels or TikToks.

Fast, accurate captioning and text-overlay skills.

Strong retention instincts — you understand hooks, pacing, and when to cut or zoom.

Tool proficiency — CapCut, Adobe Premiere Pro, or DaVinci Resolve.

Good written English — you'll be placing on-screen captions, so accuracy matters.

Reliable turnaround — you hit deadlines and flag issues early.

Self-directed — once you know the format, you run with minimal hand-holding.

Nice to have

Interest in or knowledge of sports.

explanatory motion graphics — animated text, simple lower-thirds.

Experience editing for educational or talking-head creators.

A feel for current short-form trends and audio conventions.

Logistics

Full-time, fully remote.

Compensation: based on experience. 

Hours: a few hours of overlap with US Pacific time for handoffs — otherwise flexible.

Ongoing, long-term role with room to grow as the channel scales.

Start: as soon as we find the right fit.

How to apply

Please do all three of these — applications missing the test edit won't be reviewed:

Send your portfolio — links to 3–5 short-form videos you personally edited.

Answer one question — in a sentence or two, tell us the single best hook you've ever cut, and why it worked.

Complete the paid test edit below.

The paid test edit

We respect your time, so the test is paid whether or not we move forward.

We'll send you one raw talking-head clip (about 60–90 seconds).

Edit it into a finished ~40-second Instagram Reel: animated captions, a strong hook treatment in the first 3 seconds, 2–3 simple b-roll or zoom 
nts, and a closing “save this” card.

Turn it around within 3 days.

We pay $30 USD for the completed test. 

We're judging three things: turnaround speed, caption and text quality, and whether you matched our format without needing detailed direction.

To apply, reply with your portfolio, your hook answer, and confirm you're available for the test edit.

title: Tutor - CRE Underwriting & Financial Modeling
description:
I'm a commercial real estate professional specializing in multifamily investment sales. I'm seeking a part-time private tutor to teach me multifamily underwriting and financial modeling the way it's taught in a university-level real estate development program — structured, rigorous, and built around a proper textbook curriculum.



This is a teaching engagement, not a one-off training session. I want someone who can guide me from fundamentals through a complete, self-built multifamily underwriting and waterfall model, with assessments along the way to prove I've actually learned the material.



At a glance:

• Role: Private tutor / instructor

• Schedule: Twice per week (two 60–90 minute remote sessions)

• Format: Fully remote via Zoom/Teams with screen sharing and Excel work-alongs

• Rate: $15/hour USD (paid via Wise)

• Start date: Immediate, upon successful interview



What You'll Be Teaching:

A structured curriculum of your own proposal, modeled on a university real estate development / real estate finance program, working out of a recognized textbook (e.g., Peter Linneman's Real Estate Finance and Investments or comparable). You will propose the syllabus and textbook in your application.



Core topic areas:

1. Foundations — time value of money, NPV/IRR/MIRR, cap rates, NOI, basis points, leverage concepts

2. Multifamily underwriting — rent rolls, market rents, vacancy and loss to lease, operating expenses and expense ratios, capital expenditures, debt terms (amortization, DSCR, loan sizing), investor pro forma conventions

3. Financial modeling in Excel — building a complete multifamily acquisition model from scratch, with sensitivity tables, scenario analysis, and clean formatting standards

4. Waterfalls and syndication math — preferred returns, return of capital, catch-up tranches, promote/carried interest, IRR-hurdle-based distribution waterfalls for LP/GP structures

5. Development topics — land/entitlement basics, ground-up feasibility analysis, construction budgeting and draws, permanent loan takeout, developer profit and developer waterfalls



Curriculum Structure Requirements:

• University-style curriculum: You will map out a semester-style syllabus with weekly topics tied to assigned textbook readings before we begin.

• Work out of a textbook: Each session should build on assigned reading and problem sets.

• Quizzes: Short quizzes at regular mile markers (roughly every 3–4 weeks) covering prior material.

• Tests/exams: Longer assessments at major milestones (mid-program and capstone), including a hands-on modeling exam where I build or repair a model under time constraint.

• Capstone project: A complete multifamily acquisition model built by me from scratch, including an equity waterfall tab, reviewed and graded by you.



Qualifications:

• Hands-on experience underwriting or acquiring multifamily assets (e.g., work at an acquisitions shop, appraisal firm, brokerage, developer, or lending institution)

• Advanced, demonstrable Excel modeling skills (clean formula design, scenario toggles, waterfall logic — no copy-paste templates)

• Practical familiarity with distribution waterfall math and GP/LP structures

• Prior tutoring, teaching, or training experience required

• Reliable high-speed internet, quiet workspace, and dual-screen setup for screen-share lessons

• Ability to commit to a fixed twice-weekly schedule for at least 3–6 months



Nice to Have:

• Familiarity with US markets and conventions (Argus, CoStar, or similar exposure is a plus but not required — this course is Excel-native)

• Experience building development / construction-draw models

• Textbook-honed problem-solving: you should be comfortable assigning and grading exercises from a real estate finance text



To Apply:

Please send

1. A resume

2. A brief summary of your multifamily underwriting/modeling experience (deals, roles, tools)

3. A proposed curriculum outline: the textbook you'd use, a week-by-week topic list

4. A sample of your modeling work (screenshots welcome; formulas visible)

5. Your availability (EST) and confirmation you can commit to two sessions per week

title: Financial Controller
description:
FINANCIAL CONTROLLER – AUSTRALIAN CONSTRUCTION

Remote | Full-Time | Long-Term | Philippines

Website: 



ABOUT US

Blitz Building Group builds premium, architect-designed homes in Sydney, Australia, with projects worth $2–5M each. We are a growing, owner-led business with a small team and high standards. We are looking for one exceptional finance professional to own our numbers and help shape how we grow.



WHY THIS ROLE IS DIFFERENT

- You run the finance function. You are not one person in a large team.

- You work directly with the two directors, and your recommendations shape real decisions.

- Your work has a visible impact: better margins, stronger cash flow and smarter buying.

- This is a long-term role built for someone who wants to grow with the business.



WHAT YOU'LL OWN

Finance and compliance

- Bookkeeping in Xero and Dext, with every cost coded to the correct job and cost code

- Accounts payable and receivable, progress claims, variations and supplier compliance

- Weekly payroll, Payday Super, STP and leave

- BAS, IAS and payroll workpapers for our external accountant

- Month-end close, reconciliations and financial controls



Cash flow and reporting

- A rolling 13-week cash flow forecast, with a weekly recommendation on what to pay

- A fortnightly report to the directors covering cash, debtors, creditors, job margins and overheads

- Ownership of the overhead budget: finding savings and keeping costs on track



Construction job costing (Wunderbuild)

- Budget vs actual vs committed cost on every job, by cost code

- Early warning of overruns, with the reason and a recommended fix

- Purchase orders, variations, progress claims and subcontractor agreements



Procurement

- Get competitive quotes for materials, negotiate price and terms, and report savings against the estimate



WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE IN YOUR FIRST 90 DAYS

- Payroll and bookkeeping running accurately and on time

- Books cleaned up and fully reconciled

- A reliable 13-week cash flow forecast and fortnightly director report in place

- Job costs tracked against the estimate on every live job



WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

You think like an owner. When you find a problem, you bring a solution and its dollar impact. You are accurate, organised and confident explaining the numbers to directors.



ESSENTIAL

- 5+ years of finance or bookkeeping experience with Australian businesses

- At least 2 years with Australian construction, building or trade businesses

- Expert Xero and Dext skills

- Construction job costing experience (Wunderbuild, Buildxact, Simpro, Procore or similar)

- Australian payroll, GST, BAS, PAYG and super, including Payday Super

- Cash flow forecasting and management reporting

- Advanced Excel or Google Sheets

- Excellent written and spoken English

- A dedicated workspace, reliable internet with a backup connection, and a backup power supply



ADVANTAGEOUS

- CPA, or an accounting or finance degree

- Financial Controller, Finance Manager or Senior Accountant experience

- Wunderbuild experience

- Residential construction and fixed-price contracts

- Procurement or supplier negotiation experience

- Process improvement and automation



HOW TO APPLY

Please complete every step. Incomplete applications won't be considered.

1. Start your application with the word CASHFLOW

2. Attach your CV

3. List each Australian construction business you have supported, your role, and the software you used

4. Record a 2–3 minute video (Loom or similar) introducing yourself and explaining how you would build a 13-week cash flow forecast for a builder

5. In 3–4 sentences, describe a time you found a cost or cash flow problem, what you recommended, and the result



OUR PROCESS

1. Application review

2. Paid practical test (Xero reconciliation, job cost review and a cash flow exercise)

3. Video interview with the Managing Director

4. Reference checks with at least two Australian employers or clients, plus NBI clearance

5. Offer

title: Amazon SEO Manager

This person owns the SEO engine that compounds: better indexing, better rankings, higher CTR, higher CVR, and a stronger organic share of sales—without sacrificing brand quality or compliance.



They run a disciplined cadence of keyword research and refresh, systematically improve listings (titles/bullets/A+/images/backend), and translate data (DR/DD/SQP/SI) into prioritized action. They partner closely with PPC and creative to ensure keyword targets, positioning, and content work together—especially during seasonality, deal events, and pricing shifts.



ONE THING: Drive organic ranking, discoverability, and conversion through consistent keyword research, listing optimization, and SEO execution.

Keyword Research & Keyword Refresh System

description:

We run a growing network of YouTube and TikTok channels, including a large Minecraft channel built around mod and modpack guides. Our content is search-driven: we make videos that help people find, install and enjoy modded Minecraft. You'd be joining a small, friendly team of creators.

You'll create clear, engaging guide-style videos on mods and modpacks, and you'll set the standard for quality on the Minecraft side of the business. Modded Minecraft is the priority. Consistent work is available for the right person

 staging first, code review, and no secrets or keys in code

• At least 3 years of full stack experience: front end (HTML, CSS, JavaScript or TypeScript, React or similar) and back end (Node.js, Python or PHP)

• Daily, hands-on use of AI coding tools, and the judgement to check, test and correct their output

• Experience building features or automations with LLM APIs (Anthropic, OpenAI or similar)

• Experience with REST or GraphQL APIs, SQL databases and a clean Git workflow

• A good eye for clean, mobile-friendly pages

• Clear written English, and the ability to explain technical trade-offs to non-technical teammates

• A plus: Shopify development (Liquid, Admin API), and experience with Wix or WordPress



You do not need to be a graphic designer. Visuals can be created with AI tools using our design guidelines.

• Monday to Friday

• Why you are leaving your last job or what you were doing just before this application

My resume is here:

Video introduction here:

Loo Yi

title: Experienced E-Commerce Sales  $5/hr
description:
Let's get one thing straight: this position isn't for beginners.



We're looking for someone who already understands sales, knows how to handle prospects, and can confidently close deals.



We're offering a $5/hour base rate because we want someone who can bring real sales experience to the table.



What you'll be doing:

Your responsibilities include:



Prospecting and reaching out to potential clients.



Working with cold and warm leads.



Pitching our offers through calls,
s, and direct messages.



Identifying customer pain points and presenting solutions.



Handling objections and negotiating with prospects.



Following up strategically instead of letting opportunities go cold.



Closing deals and consistently improving your sales numbers.



We want someone who knows how to move a conversation forward and confidently ask for the sale.



What you need to bring:



1. Proven Sales Experience



You understand sales psychology, pitching, objection handling, follow-up strategies, and closing techniques.



2. Real E-Commerce Experience



You know how e-commerce businesses operate, how online stores generate revenue, and the challenges business owners face.



You should be comfortable having actual business conversations with e-commerce prospects.



3. Numbers to Back It Up



We don't want to hear that you're a "natural salesperson" without anything to support it.



Show us your:



Previous sales results.



Closing rates.



Revenue generated.



Average deal size.



Biggest deal closed.



If you don't have exact numbers for everything, explain what you can confidently verify.



4. Independent and Competitive



You take ownership of your pipeline, know how to manage your time, and constantly look for ways to improve your performance.



Compensation



$5/hour base pay



Strong commission structure



Performance-based earning potential



We value people who can consistently bring results.



How to Apply



Here's your first test.



Put "BUILT TO CLOSE" as the very first line of your application.



If you miss this instruction, we'll assume you didn't read the job post.



Also, include a link to a 2-minute Loom video with your camera ON.

If your Loom shows us you know what you're doing, we'll move straight to an interview.



We're looking for closers, not people who just want to put "Sales Representative" on their resume.

title: Orthodontic Virtual Assistant (Remote -  $7 to $8 per hour)
description:
Dental office or practice experience required



Orthodontic Virtual Assistant. For someone whose voice makes a nervous parent smile before they ever walk through our door.



Our best days start with good music playing low and a phone that keeps ringing in the best way. Every caller

hears someone who sounds genuinely glad they called. By the end of the day, people who dialed in unsure have

a first visit on the calendar and are already looking forward to it. Nobody is rushing. Nobody sounds like they're

reading a script. Dr. B and the team are in sync, and the day moves like a great set: everyone knows their part,

and the whole room sounds better because of it. You'll be working virtually, but you are still part of that room.



We are small by choice. That means you will know our patients and families by name, they will know your voice,

and the people you work with will notice when you do something great and say so out loud. We're a brand new

practice in Green Hills, Nashville, and you will be one of the very first voices people hear. We're building

something we are really proud of, one great phone call at a time!



Everything we do runs on five values we call MAGIC: Mastery, Authenticity, Growth, Integrity, and Compassion.



They aren't a poster on the wall. They're how we show up for our patients and for each other, and they're what

we look for in every person who joins us.



Who thrives here

You're someone who lives our five values without being told, and who lights up when the phone rings:



Mastery. You take pride in a clean, well run schedule and a perfectly confirmed appointment, and you would

rather ask "why do we do it this way?" than guess. New software and a really good system give you a little

thrill, and insurance language sounds like something you'd enjoy learning, not something to fear.



Authenticity. You're the same warm, upbeat person on a call as you are with your best friend. Your energy

is natural, not performed. You can make a worried parent and a shy teenager both feel like the most

interesting caller of the day, and you tell the truth kindly, whether that's "that time is taken, but here's a great

option" or "here's what I'd do differently."



Growth. You're curious, you welcome change, and you hear "small team" and think "my ideas will be

heard," not "that sounds like a lot."



Integrity. You do the right thing when no one is watching. When you promise a callback, you call back. You

show up on time and ready because the first caller of the day is counting on you, and when you make a

mistake you say so and fix it.



Compassion. You can hear the worry in someone's voice and slow down before anyone asks you to. You

listen first, because every patient and family calls with different needs and different questions.

Your phone presence is the job. A caller meets us through your voice, and a warm, upbeat, confident

one is the best first impression we could ask for. If you light up on a call, we want to meet you.



Dental experience is required, and orthodontic experience is a bonus. Phone based customer service

experience helps too. Insurance experience is not required, because we will train you. Energy and heart are the

things we can't teach, and everything else we can. If you have both, we want to hear from you!



What you'll do

This role is more than scheduling. Here is what your days cover, and we will train you on the insurance side.



Patient Communication

Make outbound calls to patients as needed

Communicate professionally with patients and families

Follow scripts and practice protocols while sounding natural

Escalate questions or concerns to the appropriate team member

Maintain a positive, patient first tone on all calls



Observation and Follow Up Scheduling

Contact patients who need to schedule follow up appointments

Support observation recall and pending appointment follow up

Speak with patients in a warm, professional, and helpful way

Help patients understand next steps and get scheduled

Document call outcomes and follow up needs accurately



Insurance Verification

Verify dental and orthodontic insurance eligibility and benefits

Confirm coverage, deductibles, maximums, waiting periods, and limitations

Complete accurate insurance breakdowns

Document insurance details clearly in the practice management system

Flag missing, unclear, or incorrect insurance information for follow up



Claims Follow Up

Follow up on unpaid, denied, rejected, or delayed claims

Contact insurance companies as needed to check claim status

Review EOBs and identify payment discrepancies

Document claim updates clearly for the team

Help keep insurance and billing workflows moving accurately



What a star looks like at six months

Here are the three things on your scorecard. Hit these and you're not just doing the job, you're the reason our

days feel the way they do.

1. Every call feels like the best call of the patient's day. Phones are answered quickly and warmly, new

patient inquiries turn into booked first visits, and callers feel heard before they hang up. Families mention

your voice by name, and so do our reviews.

2. The schedule is full, smooth, and honest. Appointments are confirmed, reschedules are handled with a

smile, and missed visits get a friendly follow up. Dr. B's day flows without gaps or chaos, and the team never

wonders what's coming next.

3. You've grown into the insurance side and made us better. After our training, you can explain the basics

of orthodontic benefits to a family in plain words and know exactly when to bring in a teammate. You've also

brought us at least one idea that improved how we answer calls or run the schedule, and we put it in place.



Straight talk, up front

We'd rather you know everything now than be surprised later.



The schedule. This is a full time virtual assistant role, 40 hours a week, working remotely from your own

home office in the Philippines on US Central Time hours to match our Nashville office. That means a night

shift on your end, so this role is for Philippines based candidates who are comfortable working nights. You'll

be a true part of our team, not a faceless voice on a line. Your exact hours: 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Central

Time, Monday through Friday, with a one hour unpaid lunch.



The phone is the job. Much of your day is spent on the phone with patients and insurance companies, both

answering calls and making them. This is not a quiet, heads down,
 only seat. If you would rather avoid

the phone, this isn't the one for you.

Your voice has to come through clearly. You'll need clear, natural, confident spoken English, a quiet

space to work, reliable high speed internet, and a good headset.

We will train you on insurance. You don't need to know it already. You do need to be willing to learn it.

We're new. Some systems are still being built. Some days will be packed and some will be quiet, and

everyone pitches in on whatever needs doing, including the unglamorous stuff.

You'll hear the truth. We'll tell you what's working and what isn't, and we expect the same back.

The pay. $7 to $8 an hour.



How to apply

When you apply, please include one sentence about one time you dealt with an unreasonable or unhappy

person and turned it into a great situation. Write it the way you would say it on the phone, and put it at the very

top of your application message. Without that sentence, we won't be able to consider you.



Please submit the following:

1. A viewable link to your updated resume

2. A short paragraph describing your experience with:

Dental or orthodontic insurance verification

Patient scheduling or phone communication

3. A list of any dental, orthodontic, billing, or phone systems you have used

4. A short voice or video introduction via Vocaroo, Loom, or a similar platform so we can evaluate phone

readiness and communication style



Subject line: Orthodontic VA: Insurance & Scheduling | [Your Full Name]



We can't wait to hear from you

title: Property Maintenance Coordinator
description:

Job Type: Full-Time 

Work Hours: Monday to Friday, 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM Eastern Time, with a 30-minute break 

Job Overview:  

We are seeking a detail-oriented and proactive Maintenance Coordinator to oversee work order 

management and maintenance coordination for a portfolio of multifamily residential properties. 

In this role, you will manage the maintenance workflow from the initial resident request through 

completion and follow-up, ensuring that work orders are properly assigned, tracked, 

documented, and closed only after the work is completed. 

You will work closely with the Regional Property Manager, onsite maintenance technicians, 

residents, and vendors to monitor progress, coordinate repairs, manage outstanding work 

orders, and maintain clear visibility into maintenance operations across multiple properties. The 

ideal candidate has hands-on experience with U.S. property management operations, strong 

proficiency in AppFolio, and excellent organizational and communication skills. This role 

requires consistent follow-through, attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple work 

orders while ensuring timely service and resident satisfaction. 

Key Responsibilities: 

● Work Order Management & Tracking 

○ Audit existing open work orders across assigned properties, verify their status, 

resolve outdated or invalid entries, and establish an accurate backlog. 

○ Review new work orders in AppFolio daily, acknowledge resident requests, and 

assign tasks to the appropriate maintenance technicians or vendors. 

○ Prepare and distribute daily work order assignments to technicians and track 

progress against assigned tasks. 

○ Monitor approximately 15–20 work orders per day across multiple properties, 

following up on overdue items and resolving delays to ensure timely completion. 

○ Coordinate multi-step maintenance jobs, including parts orders, return visits, and 

repairs requiring multiple stages of work. 

○ Ensure work orders are closed only after completion is confirmed and the 

necessary notes are recorded. 

● Maintenance & Vendor Coordination 

○ Coordinate and track unit turn maintenance activities with onsite teams to help 

ensure units are ready on schedule. 

○ Dispatch approved vendors within established spending limits and escalate 

expenses exceeding authorized thresholds to management. 

○ Request and collect vendor bids as needed, following management's guidelines 

and approval procedures. 

○ Collect vendor invoices, match them to the corresponding work orders, and 

submit them to accounting promptly. 

○ Follow up on after-hours emergency work orders the next business day to 

confirm completion and document any overtime for management review. 

● Resident Communication & Service 

○ Contact residents by phone or text after completed work orders to confirm 

satisfaction and identify unresolved concerns. 

○ Communicate maintenance updates, service arrangements, and follow-up 

requirements clearly and professionally using the client's designated VoIP phone 

and messaging system. 

○ Escalate resident concerns, unresolved service issues, and recurring 

maintenance problems to the appropriate manager. 

● Reporting & Administrative Support 

○ Prepare daily and weekly reports on open, assigned, overdue, and completed 

work orders by property and technician, including productivity trends and 

outstanding issues. 

○ Maintain accurate records of vendor activity, invoices, and follow-up actions 

using AppFolio and other relevant systems. 

○ Use
 and Google Workspace or Microsoft Office tools to communicate with 

stakeholders, prepare reports, and support administrative tasks. 

○ Identify opportunities to improve maintenance tracking, documentation, and 

coordination processes. 

Required Skills & Qualifications: 

● At least two years of property maintenance coordination experience with U.S. property 

management companies; multifamily residential experience is strongly preferred. 

● Hands-on experience using AppFolio for work order management and property 

maintenance coordination is required. 

● Strong understanding of U.S. property management maintenance workflows, including 

repairs, work orders, vendor coordination, and unit turns. 

● Experience coordinating with onsite maintenance technicians and external vendors, 

monitoring task completion, and ensuring accountability. 

● Ability to manage multiple work orders across several properties, prioritize urgent 

requests, and follow through consistently. 

● Excellent written and verbal English communication skills for interacting with residents, 

vendors, technicians, and property management teams. 

● Strong attention to detail and ability to maintain accurate documentation, identify 

discrepancies, and escalate unresolved issues appropriately. 

● Experience coordinating vendor bids, reviewing invoices against work orders, and 

following established spending limits and approval procedures. 

● Proficiency in phone and text communication,
, and Google Workspace or 

Microsoft Office tools. 

● Ability to work independently and maintain a resident-focused approach to maintenance 

coordination and service resolution. 

Note: An NBI or police clearance will be required upon acceptance of the job offer.

title: Experienced Credit Repair Specialist ChexSystems, Inquiry Removal & Furnisher Relations

Document conversations, reference numbers, outcomes and next steps.

Hard Inquiry Removal

Understand bureau-specific inquiry dispute procedures.

Monitor inquiry dispute results and follow-up requirements.

ChexSystems & Consumer Banking Reports

Identify negative banking history, account closures and reporting discrepancies.

Prepare appropriate disputes for inaccurate banking information.

Communicate with financial institutions and reporting agencies.

Monitor disputes, responses and investigation results.

CRM & Client Management

Track dispute rounds, correspondence and investigation results.

Previous hands-on experience in the U.S. credit repair industry.

Advanced credit report interpretation skills.

Strong understanding of Experian, Equifax and TransUnion.

Experience communicating directly with data furnishers and creditors.

Hands-on inquiry removal experience.

Working knowledge of ChexSystems and banking-related disputes.

Explain your experience with hard inquiry removal and how you determine whether an inquiry has a legitimate basis for dispute.

When would you escalate a credit reporting issue to the CFPB?

Which credit repair software, credit monitoring platforms and phone systems have you personally used?

Qualified applicants will be required to complete a live interview, phone call role-play and practical credit report assessment without AI assistance.

title: Marketing Assistant
description:

D2C is a shopper, field and brand marketing agency operating across Australia and New Zealand. 

We are looking for a reliable, detail focused Virtual Assistant to keep our website and social channels current, consistent and professionally presented.



The role

You will manage content publishing across our WordPress website, LinkedIn and Instagram, turning supplied copy and imagery into polished, approved posts.

Our target is three core content pieces per week, adapted across all three channels. This means approximately three website uploads, three LinkedIn posts and three Instagram posts, rather than nine separate pieces of original content.

Content will include case studies, company news, campaign highlights and industry insights.



Key responsibilities



WordPress content management

Upload, format and publish case studies, news and insights using our existing website templates. Prepare featured images, headings, links, categories and image alt text. Add basic SEO titles and descriptions where supported, optimise image sizes, and check desktop and mobile presentation before publishing.



LinkedIn and Instagram publishing

Adapt supplied content into captions suited to each platform and D2C’s tone of voice. Resize and crop imagery using existing assets and templates, add appropriate tags and links, and schedule or publish approved posts. Check that published content displays correctly.



Content coordination and quality control

Maintain a simple content calendar covering drafts, approvals and publication dates. Proofread all content, organise assets and flag missing information early. Obtain approval before publishing, particularly for client names, campaign results and imagery. Provide a brief weekly update with published links, outstanding items and time spent.



What we are looking for

• Proven WordPress publishing experience, including formatting articles, managing images and working within existing templates.

• Experience managing business LinkedIn and Instagram accounts, including adapting captions and scheduling organic content.

• Strong written English and attention to detail, with the ability to follow brand guidelines and use British/Australian spelling.

• Basic image editing skills, using Canva or similar tools, plus reliable communication and the ability to meet deadlines independently.



Experience supporting a marketing agency or other business audience would be an advantage. Coding and website development experience are not required.



Working arrangements and scope

The role is expected to require approximately ten hours per week, with flexible scheduling and some availability during Sydney business hours for coordination.



D2C will provide core copy, imagery, brand guidance and approvals. Your focus will be publishing, light copy editing and adapting existing assets.



Original article writing, substantial graphic design, video production, paid advertising, ongoing community management and website development are outside the initial scope. Any additional work or hours must be agreed in advance.



How to apply

Please provide a brief introduction, your hourly rate and currency, time zone, weekly availability and relevant WordPress and social media examples. Explain your specific contribution to each example.



Success in this role means accurate, well presented content published on schedule, with minimal supervision and within the agreed hours.

title: Home Health Coder – ICD-10-CM, OASIS-E2 & PDGM (HCS-D preferred)

What you will do:

- Code home health periods in ICD-10-CM from SOC, ROC and recert OASIS assessments and referral documents, following the ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines and PDGM rules.

- Choose and sequence primary and secondary diagnoses that the record supports, and avoid codes that return to provider.

- Review OASIS-E2 answers for accuracy against the clinical record, and flag issues to clinicians through the agency's EMR.

- Check that the plan of care matches the diagnoses, orders, disciplines and visit frequencies.

- Help with QA chart reviews when needed.

- Work directly in agency EMRs (WellSky/Kinnser, Axxess, HCHB or similar).



Must have:

- 2+ years coding for U.S. home health agencies (hospital, clinic or pro-fee coding alone does not qualify).

- A current coding credential: HCS-D, BCHH-C, CPC or CCS.

- Strong working knowledge of PDGM, OASIS-E/E2 and the ICD-10-CM guidelines.

- Clear written English for coding notes and queries to U.S. clinicians.

- Reliable internet, a private workspace and availability during U.S. Pacific business hours.

- Willing to pass our HIPAA and cyber security training before getting access to any client system.

- Willing to work only inside our secure cloud workstation, never on a personal computer or phone, and to sign our confidentiality and HIPAA agreements.

- COS-C

2. Attach your resume and your coding credential, including the credential number so we can verify it.

3. Answer the five questions below in your own words, without AI tools. Do not include any real patient names, dates or record numbers.



Shortlisted applicants will complete a short coding test.



Screening questions:

1. Which home health EMRs have you coded in, for how long, and about how many charts do you code per day?

2. Under PDGM, what five factors place a 30-day period into a payment group?

3. Name two types of diagnosis codes that cause a home health claim to return to provider if listed as primary, with one example code of each.

4. A patient is admitted to home health after ORIF of a traumatic left hip fracture. They also have type 2 diabetes with diabetic polyneuropathy and use insulin daily. Which codes would you assign, in what order, and why?

5. What is the difference between a low and a high comorbidity adjustment under PDGM?

title: Remote Home Health Scribe – Clinical Documentation (Part-Time)
description:
About EZ Scribe LLC:

EZ Scribe LLC supports U.S. home health nurses with their clinical documentation. Nurses spend hours charting after every patient visit, and our scribes take that work off their plate so they can focus on patient care. Our mission is simple: reduce nurse burnout, improve accuracy, and give nurses their time back.



Position Overview:

This is a part-time, fully remote independent contractor role (about 20 hours per week), with the possibility of more hours after training. This is not a passive scribe position. You will turn nurse visit information into complete, accurate, and compliant documentation in the patient's electronic medical record (EMR), working inside EZ Scribe's secure systems.



What You Will Do:

- Review visit information submitted by home health nurses through EZ Scribe's secure systems

- Check it for completeness, accuracy, and clinical clarity, and ask for clarification when something is missing or doesn't add up

- Enter clean, organized, compliant documentation into the agency's EMR

- Learn and apply OASIS documentation standards (training provided)

- Review wound photos as part of documentation (you must be comfortable seeing wounds of varying severity)

- Communicate with your Team Lead and the nurses to resolve documentation issues

- Stay productive without constant supervision: when work slows down, check for pending items and follow up on incomplete documentation



Schedule:

- About 20 hours per week, scheduled between 9:00 AM and 5:00 PM U.S. Pacific time (1:00 AM to 9:00 AM Philippine time). Hours are flexible.

- Time is tracked with our time-tracking phone app



Pay:

- $4.00 to $6.00 per hour based on experience, paid every two weeks

- This is an independent contractor role



HIPAA and Data Security (required):

You will handle protected health information (PHI) for U.S. patients. Protecting it is a non-negotiable part of this job.

- All work is done only inside the secure EZ Scribe Cloud PC we provide. No patient information is ever saved, copied, printed, photographed, or sent outside our systems.

- You must pass HIPAA training and a cyber security training before you receive access to any systems. Training is provided if you are not already certified.

- You will sign a confidentiality agreement and our contractor agreements before starting.

- You must provide an NBI clearance issued within the last 6 months.

- You must work in a private, quiet space where no one else can see your screen.



Requirements:

- Strong written English and reading comprehension

- Exceptional attention to detail: you catch what is missing, inconsistent, or doesn't add up

- Critical thinking: you can tell when something doesn't look right clinically and ask about it

- Ability to learn new EMR and charting systems quickly and work independently

- Typing speed of at least 45 words per minute with high accuracy

- Your own reliable computer, a smartphone, and high-speed internet

- A backup internet connection and backup power for outages

- Comfort working with clinical language and wound photos



Preferred Qualifications:

- U.S. home health experience, especially familiarity with OASIS (strongly preferred)

- A background in nursing, healthcare, or allied health

- Experience with electronic medical record systems (training on our systems is provided)

- Experience in medical scribing, medical transcription, or healthcare documentation



What We Offer:

- A fully remote position

- Structured training and onboarding, including OASIS and HIPAA

- Team Lead support and ongoing guidance

- Room to grow with EZ Scribe LLC

- Purpose-driven work that makes a real difference for home health nurses and their patients



How to Apply:

1. Write EZ CHART as the first line of your application. Applications without it will not be reviewed.

2. Attach your resume.

3. In a short introduction, tell us about any home health, OASIS, medical scribing, or other healthcare documentation experience and why you're a strong fit for detail-driven documentation work.

4. Include your typing speed (words per minute) and your internet speed.



Shortlisted applicants will complete a short skills test using a practice nurse note. The practice note contains no real patient information.



Important Note:

We are looking for professionals who take initiative, think critically, and value accuracy. This is a performance-driven role where your attention to detail directly affects patient care.

title: Sports Card Research, Video Review & Data Entry Assistant
description:
Roster Reserve LLC is a U.S.-based sports-card collecting and resale business seeking a reliable, detail-oriented virtual assistant for research, video review, inventory management, and data entry. This is a part-time, long-term role. Starting pay is USD $1.50 per hour, subject to applicable wage requirements. Hours are initially 5–10 per week, with flexible scheduling and opportunities for additional hours based on performance.



PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES

• Watch recorded sports-card break videos.

• Identify cards belonging to specific teams we purchased.

• Match cards to the corresponding eBay purchase records.

• Record player names, manufacturers, sets, card numbers, parallels, serial numbers, and autographs.

• Document video timestamps and capture screenshots as supporting evidence.

• Organize findings in Google Sheets.

• Reconcile historical purchases with existing inventory.

• Flag potentially valuable or rare cards for management review.



ADDITIONAL RESPONSIBILITIES

• Research recent completed eBay sales, distinguishing sold prices from asking prices.

• Assist with inventory organization and sports-card listing descriptions.

• Perform general online research and administrative tasks.

• Use AI tools when appropriate while checking accuracy.



QUALIFICATIONS

• Excellent attention to detail, reliable internet, good written English, and Google Sheets proficiency.

• Able to follow detailed instructions and work independently.

• Sports knowledge is preferred; sports-card knowledge is a bonus, but neither is required.



Training and detailed operating procedures will be provided. Selected candidates will receive a small paid trial assignment.



APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS

Start your application with the words “Roster Reserve” to show you read the instructions, and answer all six questions:

1. What experience do you have with data entry and online research?

2. How comfortable are you using Google Sheets?

3. Are you familiar with American sports or sports cards?

4. Are you comfortable reviewing lengthy videos and documenting specific information?

5. Are you willing to accept the advertised starting hourly rate?

6. How many hours per week are you available?
